R001_stomachdrops.caption:
Dealing with a toxic boss doesn't stop when you clock out.

Your boss's name lights up your phone at 9:47 p.m. and your chest tightens before you've even read the message. You replay the meeting on the drive home. You check your email one more time before bed, just in case.

That reaction isn't you being dramatic. When work keeps putting you on guard, your body learns to stay ready. Noticing it is the first step to taking your evenings back.

Send this to the coworker who checks their phone the same way.

#ToxicBoss #ToxicWorkplace #WorkplaceAnxiety #WorkplaceMentalHealth #UnspokenAtWork

R002_reliable.caption:
You finished early. Your reward? More work. 👀

You never miss a deadline.
You never complain.
You always say yes.

So the extra project lands on your desk. Then the weekend shift. Then the new hire to train.

In healthy workplaces, reliability gets rewarded.
In toxic ones, it gets used.

Next time, don't just take it. Trade it: "I can take this on if the report moves to Monday."
That's not being difficult. It's being clear about what's possible.

Is burnout at work coming from the people who rely on you MOST? 👇

Send this to the coworker who always says yes.

C001_document.caption:
Your memory will fade. Your notes won't. 👀

The comment in front of the whole team.
The deadline that suddenly changed.
The message that crossed a line.

You tell yourself you'll remember it. Then three weeks later it's just "he's always rude to me," and that's easy to dismiss.

One incident is easy to brush off.
A dated pattern is much harder to ignore.

So write it down the same day: date, time, place, the exact words, and who was there. Calm and factual, no labels. Keep it somewhere personal that you control.
That's not being petty. It's protecting yourself. (General information, not legal advice.)

Have you ever wished you'd written something down at work? 👇

Save this for the day you need it, and send it to the coworker dealing with a bad boss right now.

R003_quickchat.caption:
Workplace anxiety has a very specific sound: a vague meeting invite from your boss with no description.

Friday, 4:55 PM. "Quick chat." Suddenly you're replaying every email from the week, and the weekend feels gone before it starts.

You're allowed to ask what it's about. "Happy to! What's it about, so I can come prepared?" is calm, professional, and gives you something solid instead of a spiral. Then do one thing tonight that's just for you.
